bio: Impressively run by two siblings, this restaurant adopted its name in homage to the chef at La Ancha, a popular restaurant in Madrid that was founded by his grandfather in the 1930s. Las Tortillas de Gabino is located in the heart of the city’s Chamberí district, where it features a cosy entrance hall, a private section, a glass-fronted wine cellar, and two contemporary dining rooms which interconnect via a corridor that leads to the kitchen, which is always visible to diners. The updated traditional menu is complemented by a superb choice of omelettes (tortillas), the most popular of which are the traditional potato-based Velazqueña, and the Trufada....
